newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia cenbank defends foreign share account law.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia cenbank defends foreign share account law.

text.p: Slovenia's central bank on Wednesday defended a ruling forcing international investors to trade through special share accounts and insisted that the move would not harm foreign interests.

Investors have interpreted the ruling, made public on Tuesday, as an attempt to clamp down on foreign trading activity and they have scrambled to offload Slovenian shares, driving the SBI index down 20 percent over the past two days.
"The step was taken in order to adapt Slovenia's banking regulations to regulations already known abroad," the Bank of Slovenia said in a short statement.
On Wednesday, the SBI closed 179.46 points lower at 1,380.66 and traders forecast the index would fall further as investors tried to fathom the ruling's details and its long-term impacts.
Foreigners had largely been behind a spectacular bull run on the Ljubljana stock exchange since the start of the year, driving the SBI up 40 percent to an all-time high.
The central bank said it was confident that the new accounts would contribute to secure and transparent administration of the market.
